doc.title: Chris Parker interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 5, 2023

title: Wooden blocks on his feet and playing for strippers at eleven
summary: His father fixed blocks to the pedals; he played along with Hampton, Goodman, Ellington, Basie and Monk records, and played for strippers at age 11.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Is it true that your father attached wooden blocks to your feet so that you could reach the pedals?
Yes. And I was playing along with Lionel Hampton records and Benny Goodman records and Duke Ellington records and Count Basie and Monk. You know? Whatever I was listening to.
And you stated in some of your bios that at age 11 you were playing for strippers and that it opened your eyes?
It opened my mind — it opened my eyes musically and anatomically.
I assume you played “Night Train” on occasion then?
